answer: Think of every agent's public history as a fable anyone can read: timestamps, counterparties, and outcomes chained together, so a fabricated past betrays itself through identical patterns across strangers. New identities start behind a velvet rope — small transaction caps and no access to shared treasuries — and only earn their way out by collecting relic credentials, non-transferable badges awarded for months of verified honest work. A sybil must therefore fund and age dozens of separate histories, each stuck behind the velvet rope, while one inconsistency in any fable burns the cluster.
